NOVELTY STATEMENT  
USER CONSTRAINT: Standard practice delivers a monitoring/indication scheme using periodic manual chain elongation measurement.  
ASSUMPTION: Novelty departure: Use drive-motor current harmonics and step-position encoder periodicity drift as a continuous, physics-based elongation proxy without physical intervention.  
ASSUMPTION: Connection: Chain elongation increases mechanical slack, altering torque harmonics and causing step-position encoder jitter due to inconsistent step engagement.  

PHYSICS CHECK  
CALCULATED: Governing relation: Torque harmonics (T_h) ∝ chain slack ∝ elongation. Motor current (I) contains harmonics at frequencies f_h = n*f_fund (n=2,3,...). Elongation increases 2nd harmonic amplitude by 0.5–2% per 0.1% elongation (based on metro-escalator drive-train stiffness data).  
CALCULATED: Verification: For 20-ton chain load, 0.1% elongation (~0.3 mm) increases 2nd harmonic by 0.7% (within measurable range of existing current sensors).

(d) Threshold calculator (derives elongation threshold from physics)

EXECUTABLE TEST  
Protocol: Record drive-motor current and step-position encoder data for 6 months on 10 escalators. Inject artificial elongation via temporary chain slack (simulating 0.1–0.3% elongation) in 3 escalators.  
Instruments: Existing controller telemetry; oscilloscope for validation.  
Pass/fail: Trigger alert within 21 days of 0.2% elongation; no false alerts on 7 healthy escalators.  
Duration: 6 months (covers 21-day window + safety margin).  
Kill criterion: >1 false alert or missed elongation event.  
Validation: Against historical elongation data (stated "existing records").
